 Age 32 years,

 Udayashankara Road 2nd Main  Udayanagar, K.R.Puram,
 Bengaluru.

Date of offence : 09-06-2004
Offences complained : U/s. 498A, 506, 323 of IPC r/w/s 3  of and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Plea : Accused No.1 & 2 Pleaded not guilty  Final Order : Accused No.1 Acquitted

Date of Order : 06-12-2025  2  C.C.No.668/2005  *****
 The Police Sub- Inspector, Women Police Station ( South Zone) Basavanagudi, Bangalore has filed charge sheet against the accused No.1 and 2 for the offences punishable U/s. 498A,
Gayathri vs Sharavanan on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71158162/
1 506, 323 of IPC r/w/s 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. The brief facts of the prosecution case are that:
 That the accused persons respectively husband and mother in law of CW-1, accused No.1 married CW-1 on 28-12-2002 in Govindappa Kalyana Mantap, whitefield Road, Bangalore.

At the time of marriage the accused persons demanded and received dowry of Rs.80,000/- cash, gold bracelet, gold neck chain and 3 rings and also CW-1 was given long chain, necklace, ear rings,
mati, 4 finger rings etc.

When CW-1 started residing with accused at No.41 Sri Narayana Nilaya, Udayashankara Road,
Udayanagar, K.R. Puram, Bangalore after the marriage, accused was harassing her demanding her to bring dowry of house and vehicle and used to harass her and had driven her out of the  3  C.C.No.668/2005 matrimonial home.

When she was at parents home at No.31,
Jakkasandra, Sarjapura Road, Bangalore, both the accused went there and also demanded further dowry in cash, house and vehicle.

Further the accused persons assaulted her with their hands and legs, causing bodily pain and caused injuries to nose and mouth and criminally intimidated to take out her life and thereby accused persons have committed aforesaid offences.
 3. The accused No.1 and 2 were enlarged on bail.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took the cognizance of the alleged offence and furnished copy of the prosecution papers to the accused persons.

Charge for the offences P/U/S. 498A, 506, 323 of IPC r/w/s 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act was framed, read Gayathri vs Sharavanan on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71158162/
2 over and explained to the accused No.1 and 2.

sentences.text: Accused No.1 and 2 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Thereafter the matter was posted for evidence.
Later accused persons remained absent and failed to appeared before the court.
Proclamation and attachment was issued against the accused on many occasions  4  C.C.No.668/2005 and was returned unexecuted.
Permission sought to record evidence U/s.299 of cr.P.C. from the Honb'le Prl.Dist. & Sessions Judge.
A permission was accorded to record evidence U/s.299 Cr.P.C.

After recording evidence of Complainant and Head constable., it is ordered to submit the entire record before the Hon'ble City Civil & Sessions seeking permission to withdraw this case from CC register and transfer the same to LP.R..

As per request of the PSI, this case was reopened as accused No.1 was traced and hence, case is restored and issued body warrant against the accused person, after appearance of accused No.1,
he was enlarged on bail in this case .
Accused No.2 could not be secured as such, and he was separated from this case and the concerned I.O. is directed to file a splitup chargesheet against accused No.2.
4. In support of the case of prosecution, 01 witness was examined as PW1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex-P1 to 3.

As there were no incriminating evidence against the accused the  5  C.C.No.668/2005 recording of Statement of Accused as required U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C.,
was dispensed with.
5. I have heard the arguments of learned Sr.APP., for the prosecution and learned counsel for the accused.

Perused the Gayathri vs Sharavanan on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71158162/
3 materials available on record.
 6.

The following points arise for my determination:-
 1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that the accused have subjected the CW1 to  mental and physical cruelty in respect of demand of  dowry thereby accused have committed the offences  punishable U/s.498A, 506, 323 of IPC r/w/s 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
 2) what order?
 7.

My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1 ........In the Negative.
 Point No.2........

As per final order, for the following:
 REASONS
8. It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined one witness as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to  6  C.C.No.668/2005 Ex.P3 documents.
Ex.P1 is the first information statement.
Ex.P.2 is the spot panchanama.
Ex-P3 is the Wedding invitation.
9. CW-1 was examined as PW-1.
She in her examination-in- chief has supported the case of the prosecution.

However during her cross examination she has deposed that her marriage with accused No.1 was performed on 28-12-2002 and deposed after the marriage, accused looked after her well and deposed accused did not subjected her to any physical and mental cruelty, in demand of dowry and never abused, assaulted her and threatened to kill her.

She has also deposed that accused never demand any dowry Gayathri vs Sharavanan on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71158162/
4 during the marriage and also after the marriage and she pleaded her ignorance about the contents of Ex.P.1 and P.2.
 10.

On appreciation of entire materials on record, it is apparent that PW-1 being the informant, key and material witness though supported the case of the prosecution during her chief examination but has turned hostile to the prosecution case.
Therefore, this court was pleased to reject the prayer of the learned Sr.APP to summon other chargesheeted witnesses.

Even, if the summons was issued to other chargesheeted witnesses, no purpose  7  C.C.No.668/2005 would be served as the material witness has given go-bye to her own statement and also the valuable time of the court would be saved.
As such other charge sheeted witnesses were dropped and prosecution evidence was taken as closed.
In view of the material witness, turning hostile, and in the absence of evidence of material witness, the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

11. POINT No.2:- For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER Acting Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., accused No.1 is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A, 506, 323 of IPC r/w/s 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused No.1 shall stand canceled.
